Method of Attack: Malware-as-a-service targeting Android devices with file-encrypting ransomware capabilities
Encrypts all files on infected devices without file-type discrimination
Displays fake FBI ransom note accusing victim of storing adult content
Demands credit card information instead of cryptocurrency
Tricks victim into enabling Accessibility Service via fake Streaming Video Optimization alert
Uses BroadcastReceiver triggered by action.SCREEN_ON to keep device awake and WiFi on
Stores decryption key in SharedPreferences on device
Sends logs after decryption and self-deletes
Can execute commands from C2 including making calls, exporting installed apps list, deleting encryption keys, and running remote shell
Attack Vector: Distribution via instant messaging apps and social media
Indicators of Compromise: Four IP addresses used for command and control (C2) as tweeted by Tatyana Shishkova
Ransom note demanding $500 credit card payment
Use of Accessibility Service permission trick
Commands from C2 including action.SCREEN_ON broadcast
